title: Duke University (Duke)
summary: Duke University (Duke) is a university in Durham. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with Duke.

sections.heading: What Duke is known for
paragraphs: Duke University (Duke) is a private nonprofit institution known for its selective admissions process, with an admission rate of approximately 5.71%. The university has an undergraduate enrollment of 6,442 students, reflecting its moderate size and competitive academic environment. Duke is particularly recognized for its strong programs in health-related fields, which constitute about 6.11% of its academic offerings. While the university does not have a significant focus on business programs, it maintains a diverse range of disciplines within its curriculum. As a private nonprofit university, Duke emphasizes research, innovation, and comprehensive education across various fields.

sections.heading: How to read Duke tuition
paragraphs: Duke University charges the same tuition rate for both in-state and out-of-state students, which is $68,758. This uniform tuition policy means that all students pay the same amount regardless of their residency status. The total cost of attendance, which includes tuition as well as additional expenses such as fees, room, board, and other personal costs, amounts to $87,072. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and their families plan for the financial commitment required to attend Duke.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Duke University offers financial aid to help offset the cost of attendance, with approximately 14.03% of students receiving Pell Grants. Among students who complete their degrees, the median debt is $13,000, reflecting the typical borrowing amount. Prospective students can explore Duke's net price calculator and additional financial aid information on the university's official website at www.duke.edu/ or through the College Scorecard at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?198419. These resources provide valuable insights into the potential costs and aid options available.

sections.heading: Academic features
paragraphs: Duke University is known for its strong academic environment, characterized by a low student-faculty ratio of 5 to 1. This ratio allows for more personalized attention and closer interaction between students and faculty members. Such an environment fosters collaborative learning and supports a diverse range of academic programs across various disciplines. The university's commitment to maintaining a low student-faculty ratio reflects its emphasis on quality education and mentorship.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Career outcomes for graduates of Duke University (Duke) demonstrate strong post-completion success. The university reports a high completion rate of approximately 96.78% within 150% of the expected time, indicating that most students finish their degrees on time or with minimal delay. Median earnings for Duke graduates are notable, with those measured six years after completion earning around $85,792, and median earnings rising to $97,800 ten years after graduation. These figures reflect the long-term economic benefits of a Duke education. Additionally, the median debt for students who complete their degrees is approximately $13,000, suggesting a manageable level of borrowing relative to potential earnings. Overall, Duke's career outcomes highlight the institution's effectiveness in preparing students for successful and financially rewarding careers.
